LESSON: DANCE PRODUCTION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Foundations
Topic 1.7: Dance Production
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Dance Production, part of Foundations in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How are multimedia effects utilized to enhance dance production?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Dance Production together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: The learner uses digital devices with appropriate assistive technology while watching or

listening to a variety of dances.

● Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups while sourcing and designing costumes for dance

performance.

● Self-efficacy: The learner learns to apply multimedia effects in production of a dance performance.

Values:
● Patriotism: The learner takes pride in listening to a variety of Kenyan dances.

● Respect: The learner accommodates others’ ideas in group activities as they choose a dance based on a theme

of risk awareness and management on road use,

25

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Road safety: the learner chooses a dance theme based on a risk awareness and management on road use and

design an appropriate costume.

● Peer Education and Mentorship: The learner assists others in groups as they choose a dance theme.

● Social Cohesion: The learner actively participates in group work while applying multimedia effects in

production of a dance performance during a school event

● Resource Mobilization and Utilization: The learner makes proper use of popular music from the community.

Suggested Learning Resources

Traditional musical instruments, Resource persons, Costumes and props, Audio/visual recordings of dances,

Exercise books in appropriate print, ICT devices, Braille equipment and materials,

Suggested Key Skills Assessed

• Describing elements of dance

• Creating props and costumes

• Describing concepts of choreography

• Selecting multimedia effects
